findings.message: Review the accepted vulnerabilities past their date in .hecatron/config.json audit.ignore: GHSA-1 (until 2026-01-01)
findings.why: An acceptance's date is when it was to be looked at again; past it, the risk is accepted by no one.

findings.message: Fix or accept the known vulnerabilities hct audit go reported on 2026-10-27 (log .logs/audit/go.log)
findings.why: A dependency with a known vulnerability is the easiest way in; accepting one with a reason and a date keeps the decision reviewed.

findings.message: Pin each GitHub Action to a release tag or a commit, not a branch (a uses: line names @main, @master or another branch)
findings.why: A branch moves: whatever its owner pushes next runs in your CI, with your workflow's permissions and secrets.

findings.message: Install with npm ci in CI, not npm install
findings.why: npm ci installs exactly what package-lock.json records, fails when it no longer matches package.json, and is faster on a clean machine.

findings.message: Run Python's tests in CI: no CI configuration mentions it
findings.why: Tests that run only on someone's machine stop being run; CI runs them on every change.

findings.message: Move off Go 1.20 (pinned in go/go.mod): that line is past its end of life; the newest is 1.27
findings.why: Each Go release is supported until there are two newer major releases; after that it gets no security fixes.

findings.message: Add a pyproject.toml declaring the build system ([build-system]), and move the metadata from setup.py into it
findings.why: pyproject.toml is the standard place for a project's build system and metadata; without it pip falls back to setuptools' deprecated legacy path.

findings.message: Move off Python 3.8 (pinned in python/.python-version): that line is past its end of life; the newest is 3.15
findings.why: Each Python release line gets fixes for five years, then none, security fixes included.

findings.message: Update Rust 1.80 (pinned in rust/rust-toolchain.toml): it is 19 releases behind 1.99
findings.why: Rust supports only its latest stable release, which every six weeks brings fixes, including security fixes; a toolchain a year behind has none of them.

findings.message: Update typescript/package-lock.json: it doesn't record the dependencies package.json declares
findings.why: npm ci refuses to install when package-lock.json and package.json disagree; npm install updates the lock.

findings.message: Pin Node.js's version in .nvmrc (it runs 24.22.1 now, hecatron's default)
findings.why: Node.js has no version setting of its own; nvm, fnm, volta and hecatron read .nvmrc, so everyone runs the release line the project is tested on.

ignored.message: Set edition in Cargo.toml's [package] (edition = "2024", or edition.workspace = true)
ignored.why: Without an edition Cargo builds the package as Rust 2015, with that edition's older rules.
